text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former presidential economic advisor Kalonga Stambuli was arrested for allegedly misallocating funds from President Bakili Muluzi's international Appeal Fund for Clean Water, but Southern Malawi Police Commissioner Howard Mwandira declined to spell out the charges.

- Opposition Malawi Congress Party and the Alliance for Democracy (Aford) are expected to meet today in Lilongwe to synchronise their views on a technical report on the proposed merger amid mounting signs of a clear division on the issue in MCP.
- Malawi will host the Southern African Development Community (SADC) annual summit in September, the Ministry of Finance announced.
- Police arrested former presidential economic advisor Kalonga Stambuli on allegation of theft of 354,000 kwacha ($23,600) from president Bakili Muluzi, defense lawyer Gustav Kaliwo said.
- Despite the death in custrody of an accomplice in the 38 million kwacha ($2.5 million) Finance Bank fraud, the accused were again denied bail.
